meta.title: Harmonic Inc — Nimrod Ben-Natan's CableOS virtualisation pivot through the DOCSIS 4.0 cycle and the video software separation
meta.abstract: Harmonic Inc is a San Jose, California-based broadband and video technology vendor listed on the NASDAQ under the ticker HLIT. The company operates two principal business segments: Broadband, which provides the CableOS virtualised cable access platform (vCMTS) to cable operators including the substantial multi-year deployment programmes at Comcast and Charter Communications; and Video, which provides software-based video processing and delivery solutions for media customers. The 2019-2024 period was substantially defined by the CableOS deployment scaling at Comcast (the principal cable operator customer for the virtualised platform), the broader DOCSIS 4.0 transition cycle providing the multi-year forward Broadband segment demand context, and the strategic posture refinement separating the Broadband and Video segment operations including the announced 2024 spin-off planning for the Video business. Under CEO Nimrod Ben-Natan (since February 2024, succeeding interim CEO Walter Jankovic who had succeeded Patrick Harshman following his September 2023 retirement), the strategic mandate has been the CableOS deployment scaling continuation, the broader Broadband segment positioning through the DOCSIS 4.0 cycle, and the Video segment separation planning. The fiscal 2024 revenue was approximately $580 million reflecting the Broadband segment scaling combined with the Video segment trajectory; the fiscal 2025-2026 quarterly progression has continued the CableOS deployment scaling plus the broader Broadband segment positioning evolution.

chapters.title: Snapshot
chapters.body:
## A Company at an Inflection

Harmonic's strategic reset arrived later, and in a more orderly sequence, than the draft dossier suggested. On 8 April 2024 the board said Patrick Harshman would retire as president and chief executive officer effective 11 June 2024 and named Nimrod Ben-Natan, then senior vice president and general manager of Harmonic's broadband business, as his successor. There was no interim chief executive bridge: Harshman remained in the role through the handover. Ben-Natan had joined Harmonic in 1996 and had run the broadband franchise since 2012, making the succession a continuity choice around the cOS platform rather than a break with strategy. [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

That timing mattered. Harshman had been chief executive since May 2006, after joining the company in 1993, and had overseen Harmonic's long shift from broadcast-video hardware toward software-defined broadband access. Ben-Natan inherited the company precisely as operators were preparing for the next DOCSIS spending cycle and as Harmonic's board was revisiting what to do with the legacy Video business. [Harshman CEO appointment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-appoints-patrick-harshman-president-and-chief-executive) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/)

## Two Segments, Then One Pending Sale

Through the frozen window Harmonic still reported two operating lines. The Broadband business centred on cOS, the company's software-based virtualized broadband platform running on commercial off-the-shelf servers and paired with distributed-access devices for DOCSIS and fiber deployments. The Video business supplied software and appliances for video processing, playout, streaming and broadcast delivery. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm) [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

The Video story also required correction. Harmonic did not announce a 2024 spin-off or separation. It announced in October 2023 that it had begun a formal strategic review of the Video business; on 8 April 2024 it said that review had ended without a transaction because market conditions did not meet the board's value-creation objectives. The actual sale process visible inside the frozen window began much later: on 8 December 2025 Harmonic said it had received a binding offer from Leone Media Inc., doing business as MediaKind, to acquire the Video business for about $145 million in cash. By 11 May 2026 Harmonic said the French employee works council consultation had been completed on 12 March, that the company had delivered its put notice on 16 March, and that both sides had executed the asset purchase agreement on 20 March, with closing still expected in the second quarter of 2026. [Harmonic Q3 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2023-results) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Pending sale to MediaKind](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-pending-sale-its-video-business-mediakind) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## Revenue Arc and the DOCSIS Pause

The financial arc was also materially understated in the draft. Harmonic's reported revenue was $402.9 million in 2019, $378.8 million in 2020, $507.1 million in 2021, $625.0 million in 2022, $607.9 million in 2023 and a record $678.7 million in 2024. The 2024 mix was $488.2 million of Broadband revenue and $190.5 million of Video revenue. In 2025, after the Video business was classified as held for sale, total company revenue was $570.8 million, while continuing-operation Broadband revenue was $360.5 million. [2020 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131021000012/hlit-20201231.htm) [2021 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131022000012/hlit-20211231.htm) [Harmonic Q4 2022 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2022-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2023-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results)

| Fiscal year | Total revenue ($m) | Broadband ($m) | Video ($m) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 2022 | 625.0 | 350.8 | 274.2 |
| 2023 | 607.9 | 388.5 | 219.4 |
| 2024 | 678.7 | 488.2 | 190.5 |
| 2025 | 570.8 | 360.5* | held for sale |
| 2026 guidance | — | 475-495 | sale pending |

*Continuing operations only.

Management described 2025 as a timing trough rather than a broken thesis. In February 2025 Harmonic said its prudent 2025 Broadband outlook reflected shifts in customer deployment timing as operators moved toward Unified DOCSIS 4.0. By February 2026 the company said record fourth-quarter Broadband bookings of $346.9 million had driven a 3.5 book-to-bill ratio and backlog plus deferred revenue of $573.8 million, up 73 per cent year on year. In May 2026 Harmonic said first-quarter Broadband revenue had risen 43 per cent year on year to $121.7 million and raised full-year Broadband guidance to $475 million-$495 million. [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## The Comcast Anchor

Comcast remained the commercial reference account around which the Broadband story turned. Harmonic's 2016 warrant agreement with Comcast tied equity upside to CableOS and related product milestones; by 2024 Harmonic's annual report said Comcast had accounted for 44 per cent of 2023 net revenue, 39 per cent of 2022 net revenue and 26 per cent of 2021 net revenue. In September 2025 Harmonic and Comcast said Comcast had expanded its network to more than one million new locations in 2024 and planned more than 1.2 million new locations by the end of 2025 using Harmonic's converged broadband platform. By the first quarter of 2026 Harmonic said cOS had been commercially deployed with 150 customers serving 45.7 million cable modems. [Comcast warrant agreement](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-comcast-warrant-agreement) [2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131025000021/hlit-20241231.htm) [Harmonic and Comcast](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-and-comcast-work-together-expand-fiber-broadband-access) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## Dossier Questions

The questions that followed were therefore narrower and more concrete than the draft implied. Could Comcast's deployment pace remain durable enough to support Harmonic through the DOCSIS 4.0 ramp? Could Harmonic convert what it described as record backlog and a widening Rest-of-Market pipeline into a less concentrated Broadband revenue mix? Could the MediaKind transaction close on the timetable laid out in the March 2026 asset purchase agreement? And once Video was gone, would the market value Harmonic primarily as a DOCSIS-and-fiber software platform company rather than as a hybrid video-and-broadband vendor?

chapters.title: From 1988 founding through DiviCom, Comcast CableOS, Harshman, Ben-Natan
chapters.body:
## Origins in Broadband Video Infrastructure

Harmonic said in its most recent annual report that it was initially incorporated in California in June 1988 and reincorporated in Delaware in May 1995. The same filing said the company had been listed on Nasdaq since its initial public offering in 1995. Those facts matter because they locate Harmonic's origins not in the DOCSIS 4.0 era that now defines the equity story, but in the earlier build-out of digital video and broadband headend infrastructure. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm)

Patrick Harshman was part of that earlier company, but the chronology in the draft had stretched his tenure by almost a decade. Harmonic's own 2006 succession announcement said Harshman joined the company in 1993 and was appointed president and chief executive officer in May 2006. When the board announced his retirement in April 2024, it was ending an 18-year CEO run and a roughly 31-year operating career at Harmonic, not a 26-year stint in the chief executive seat. [Harshman CEO appointment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-appoints-patrick-harshman-president-and-chief-executive) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/)

## DiviCom, Corrected

The DiviCom chapter also needed substantial repair. Harmonic did complete the acquisition of the DiviCom business of C-Cube Microsystems, but the closing took place on 3 May 2000, not in 1999, and Harmonic's 2000 annual-report disclosures later recorded the purchase price at roughly $1.8 billion, including about $1.6 billion of stock issued, $155 million of options assumed and $9.6 million of transaction expense. [Harmonic 2000 annual-report excerpt](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000089161802001226/f78639e10-k.htm) [DiviCom completion filing](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/static-files/4a31b16e-c1ae-4670-8312-5843e6fc35ef)

Just as important, Nimrod Ben-Natan did not join Harmonic through that deal. Harmonic's current governance page said he joined the company in 1996, was promoted to vice president of product marketing, solutions and strategy in 2007, and became senior vice president and general manager of Cable Products in June 2012. Before Harmonic he worked at Orckit Communications and earlier in the Israeli Defense Signal Corps. The draft's repeated claim that he entered through DiviCom was unsupported by Harmonic's own current biography and has been removed. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

That correction changes the way the succession story reads. Ben-Natan's legitimacy came not from having arrived with a blockbuster acquisition, but from having spent nearly three decades inside Harmonic's own engineering and product organisation, including the period in which the company moved from video infrastructure into software-defined broadband access. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

## Building cOS and the Comcast Link

The strategic inflection that defined Harmonic's 2020s position began in the CableOS period. On 26 September 2016 Harmonic entered into a warrant agreement with Comcast under which Comcast could purchase up to 7,816,162 shares based on specific CableOS and other product sales and deployment milestones, at an exercise price of $4.76 per share. The structure was unusual for a listed infrastructure vendor and amounted to an early commercial endorsement of Harmonic's virtualized cable-access strategy. [Comcast warrant agreement](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-comcast-warrant-agreement) [Warrant exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131016000104/hlit-201609268xkcomcastwar.htm)

Commercial deployments followed. Harmonic's 2018 and later broadband press releases described CableOS as the industry's first software-based CMTS and by November 2018 said regional operators such as TVS Cable were using it for DOCSIS 3.1 launches. Harmonic's more recent Comcast release said the two companies were using the platform together as Comcast expanded into new fiber and DOCSIS locations, while Harmonic's 2025 and 2026 results showed cOS scaling from 142 customers and 37.6 million cable modems at the end of the third quarter of 2025 to 150 customers and 45.7 million cable modems in the first quarter of 2026. [TVS Cable deployment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/tvs-cable-deploys-docsis-31-broadband-offering-harmonics/) [Harmonic Q3 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2025-results) [Harmonic and Comcast](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-and-comcast-work-together-expand-fiber-broadband-access) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

The revenue line moved with that rollout. Harmonic's reported revenue was $402.9 million in 2019, $378.8 million in 2020, $507.1 million in 2021, $625.0 million in 2022, $607.9 million in 2023 and $678.7 million in 2024. The draft had understated every year in that sequence. [2020 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131021000012/hlit-20201231.htm) [2021 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131022000012/hlit-20211231.htm) [Harmonic Q4 2022 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2022-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2023-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results)

| Fiscal year | Total revenue (USD m) |
|---|---:|
| 2019 | 402.9 |
| 2020 | 378.8 |
| 2021 | 507.1 |
| 2022 | 625.0 |
| 2023 | 607.9 |
| 2024 | 678.7 |

The more precise segment picture is instructive. In 2022 Harmonic generated $350.8 million of Broadband revenue and $274.2 million of Video revenue. In 2023 the split was $388.5 million and $219.4 million. In 2024 it was $488.2 million and $190.5 million. Broadband had become the growth engine before the Video divestiture discussion turned into a transaction. [Harmonic Q4 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2023-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results)

## Governance, Strategic Review and Succession

The governance timeline also needed correction. Patrick Gallagher had been a Harmonic director since October 2007 and was elected board chair in April 2013, according to the company's governance page; he did not become chair in 2022. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

The Video story unfolded in two stages. On 30 October 2023 Harmonic said it had initiated a formal strategic review of the Video business. On 8 April 2024 it said the review had concluded without a transaction and that the go-forward plan was to drive profitable growth in Video through focus and cost discipline. Only in December 2025 did that posture turn into a signed path to exit, when Harmonic said it had received MediaKind's binding offer and had entered into the related put-option structure. [Harmonic Q3 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2023-results) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Pending sale to MediaKind](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-pending-sale-its-video-business-mediakind)

Ben-Natan's move into the top job was similarly more linear than the draft implied. Harmonic announced the succession on 8 April 2024, kept Harshman in place through 11 June 2024, and then put Ben-Natan into the president and chief executive role on that date. Harmonic's second-quarter 2024 filing separately disclosed a consulting agreement with Harshman effective 11 June 2024, underscoring that he had retired from management rather than remaining a director through 2026. [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Q2 2024 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131024000074/hlit-20240628.htm)

Seen in that sequence, Harmonic's history was not the story of a 1990s-era video company abruptly broken apart in 2024. It was the slower story of a listed infrastructure vendor that had spent almost a decade commercializing software-based broadband access, used the Video business as a cash-generative legacy line while broadband scaled, tested strategic alternatives in late 2023 and early 2024 without acting, and only after another record year in 2024 committed to the MediaKind sale that would make Harmonic a broadband-only company if closed.

chapters.title: Broadband (CableOS), Video segment being separated, and DOCSIS 4.0 context
chapters.body:
## The Architecture Shift: Software Replaces Proprietary Chassis

Harmonic's broadband thesis rested on a specific architectural bet. In Harmonic's own filings, cOS was described as a software-based broadband access solution that ran on commercial off-the-shelf servers connected to distributed access nodes. In practice that meant shifting CMTS intelligence out of proprietary headend hardware and into cloud-native software, while pairing it with remote PHY and optical-line-terminal devices that could support both DOCSIS and fiber evolution. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm) [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

That architecture mattered economically because it changed the cadence of upgrades. Instead of treating broadband access as a sequence of appliance swaps, operators could add compute on standard servers, push software features at shorter intervals and converge DOCSIS and fiber management around the same core. Harmonic's product announcements during the frozen window repeatedly marketed cOS in precisely those terms: a common control layer for next-generation DOCSIS and fiber networks, not a single-purpose hardware box. [Harmonic Extends Lead in Virtualized Broadband](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-extends-lead-virtualized-broadband/) [Harmonic Defines a New Era of Broadband Connectivity at ANGA COM 2026](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-defines-new-era-broadband-connectivity-anga-com-2026)

## Comcast as Proving Ground, 2016-2026

The commercial proving ground for that model was Comcast. Harmonic's 2016 warrant agreement with Comcast tied equity vesting to CableOS and related-product milestones, which effectively marked Comcast out as the anchor account before volume deployment was visible in the reported numbers. By September 2025 Harmonic and Comcast were describing a partnership that had extended beyond DOCSIS capacity to fiber expansion into new markets, with more than one million new Comcast locations added in 2024 and more than 1.2 million targeted by the end of 2025. [Comcast warrant agreement](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-comcast-warrant-agreement) [Harmonic and Comcast](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-and-comcast-work-together-expand-fiber-broadband-access)

The scale of the platform's installed base confirmed that this was no longer an early-adopter story. Harmonic said cOS was commercially deployed with 121 customers serving 32.0 million cable modems by the third quarter of 2024, 142 customers serving 37.6 million modems by the third quarter of 2025, 146 customers and 41.3 million modems by year-end 2025, and 150 customers and 45.7 million modems by the first quarter of 2026. [Harmonic Q3 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q3 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2025-results) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## Revenue Mix and the 2025 Pause

The draft had read the 2024-2025 shape too pessimistically and with the wrong base figures. Harmonic's consolidated revenue rose to $678.7 million in 2024 from $607.9 million in 2023, with Broadband contributing $488.2 million and Video $190.5 million. The real break came in 2025, when the company reported $570.8 million of total revenue and only $360.5 million of continuing-operation Broadband revenue as customer deployment timing shifted during the move toward Unified DOCSIS 4.0. [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results)

That did not, however, look like a collapse in market relevance. In February 2026 Harmonic said fourth-quarter Broadband bookings had reached $346.9 million, producing a 3.5 book-to-bill ratio and $573.8 million of backlog plus deferred revenue. Three months later it said first-quarter Broadband revenue had risen 43 per cent year on year to $121.7 million and lifted Broadband backlog plus deferred revenue to $582.1 million. [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## DOCSIS 4.0: Why the Upgrade Cycle Mattered

Harmonic's relevance to DOCSIS 4.0 also needed more precise sourcing. On 17 October 2023 Harmonic said cOS, previously branded CableOS, had added unified DOCSIS 4.0 support spanning full duplex and extended-spectrum variants, alongside 10G fiber support, simplified timing synchronization and other operational upgrades. In September 2024 Harmonic and Comcast said they would demonstrate what they called the industry's first unified DOCSIS 4.0 and fiber solution at SCTE TechExpo24. In July 2025 Harmonic said it had recorded 14 Gbps downstream performance at a CableLabs interoperability event. [Harmonic Extends Lead in Virtualized Broadband](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-extends-lead-virtualized-broadband/) [Comcast and Harmonic at SCTE TechExpo24](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/comcast-and-harmonic-demonstrate-industrys-first-unified-docsis/) [14 Gbps DOCSIS 4.0 record](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-sets-docsis-40-record-14-gbps-downstream-speed)

Those releases did not prove an industry-wide capex boom on their own. What they did prove was that Harmonic had positioned its platform as a migration path rather than as a dead-end appliance generation. That distinction was central to the management argument that 2025 represented a pause between deployment phases rather than a reversal.

## Video: Review First, Sale Later

The Video segment's timeline required equal precision. Harmonic initiated a strategic review in October 2023, ended it without a transaction in April 2024, and only on 8 December 2025 disclosed the MediaKind binding offer and put-option structure. By the first quarter of 2026 the company said the works council consultation had ended, the asset purchase agreement had been executed, and closing was still expected in the second quarter. [Harmonic Q3 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2023-results) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Pending sale to MediaKind](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-pending-sale-its-video-business-mediakind) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

That meant Harmonic entered the frozen window not as a company that had already completed a portfolio separation, but as one still operating both businesses while preparing to shed Video. The Broadband segment was already the investment case; the pending sale merely made the capital-markets story cleaner.
