chapters.body:
## A Revenue Curve Built Around Scale, Then Timing

Harmonic's financial story through the frozen window was more uneven, and more concentrated, than the draft allowed. Reported revenue was $402.9 million in 2019, $378.8 million in 2020, $507.1 million in 2021, $625.0 million in 2022, $607.9 million in 2023 and a record $678.7 million in 2024 before falling back to $570.8 million in 2025. Those figures came directly from Harmonic's annual reports and year-end earnings releases; the previously drafted 2019-2024 series materially understated every year except 2025. [2020 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131021000012/hlit-20201231.htm) [2021 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131022000012/hlit-20211231.htm) [Harmonic Q4 2022 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2022-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2023-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results)

| Fiscal year | Revenue ($m) | YoY change |
|---|---:|---:|
| 2019 | 402.9 | — |
| 2020 | 378.8 | -6.0% |
| 2021 | 507.1 | 33.9% |
| 2022 | 625.0 | 23.2% |
| 2023 | 607.9 | -2.7% |
| 2024 | 678.7 | 11.6% |
| 2025 | 570.8 | -15.9% |

The better way to read the arc was by segment and by customer concentration. Harmonic's year-end segment tables showed Broadband revenue of $350.8 million in 2022, $388.5 million in 2023 and $488.2 million in 2024, while Video revenue moved from $274.2 million to $219.4 million and then $190.5 million over the same period. Broadband had become the engine well before the Video business was reclassified as held for sale. [Harmonic Q4 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2023-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results)

## Comcast Concentration, Quantified

The draft was directionally right that one customer drove much of the volatility, but the most useful figures came from Harmonic's 2024 annual report. That filing said Comcast represented 44 per cent of 2023 net revenue, 39 per cent of 2022 net revenue and 26 per cent of 2021 net revenue. In other words, the multi-year step-up from 2021 through 2024 was not broad market diffusion; it was disproportionately the monetisation of a single anchor deployment and the adjacent credibility that deployment created. [2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131025000021/hlit-20241231.htm)

That concentration helps explain both the 2024 record and the 2025 retrenchment. In February 2025 Harmonic said its 2025 Broadband guidance reflected shifts in customer deployment timing as operators transitioned to Unified DOCSIS 4.0. By November 2025 Ben-Natan was describing stronger-than-expected orders landing earlier than planned in the third quarter, and by February 2026 he said fourth-quarter Broadband bookings had reached $346.9 million, driving a 3.5 book-to-bill ratio and substantially higher backlog. [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q3 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2025-results) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results)

## Backlog, Guidance and the Rebound Signal

The clearest leading indicators inside the frozen window were backlog and forward guidance rather than the depressed 2025 revenue line by itself. Harmonic ended fiscal 2025 with $573.8 million of backlog and deferred revenue, versus $332.3 million a year earlier, and said current backlog alone had risen 110 per cent to $307 million. On 11 May 2026 it reported first-quarter Broadband revenue of $121.7 million, first-quarter bookings of $115.9 million, and backlog plus deferred revenue of $582.1 million. Management raised full-year 2026 Broadband guidance to $475 million-$495 million. [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

Those figures did not eliminate the lumpiness. They did, however, support the company's claim that 2025 had been a timing trough around Unified DOCSIS 4.0 rather than a structural loss of relevance.

## Capital Structure and Financial Flexibility

The capital-structure section also required a narrower and more accurate treatment. Harmonic priced a $105.0 million offering of 2.00 per cent convertible senior notes due 2024 in September 2019 and granted an option for an additional $10.5 million, which is why later disclosures referred to $115.5 million of 2024 notes outstanding. In May 2020 the company separately exchanged about $36.8 million of its 2020 convertible notes into 4.375 per cent convertible notes due 2022. [2019 convert offering](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-inc-announces-pricing-offering-105-million-convertible) [2020 note exchange](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-inc-announces-exchange-convertible-notes)

By late 2023 Harmonic had also arranged a new $160 million credit facility, explicitly noting that it provided flexibility around the 2024 convertible maturity and share repurchases. In the second quarter of 2024 the company reported repayment of $115.5 million of convertible debt in its cash-flow statement. In February 2025 the board authorised a new three-year $200 million stock-repurchase programme, and in the first quarter of 2026 Harmonic said it had repurchased roughly 4.2 million shares for $43.0 million. [New credit facility](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-new-160-million-credit-facility) [Harmonic Q2 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-second-quarter-2024-results) [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## The Video Sale Framework

The separation framework itself also needed factual repair. Harmonic did not spend 2024 executing a decided spin-off. It spent late 2023 and early 2024 reviewing alternatives, stayed put in April 2024, and only on 8 December 2025 entered the MediaKind put-option structure. Harmonic's 2025 10-K said the put option gave the company the right to require Leone Media Inc. to buy the Video business for $145 million in cash, subject to working-capital, cash, debt and specified-selling-expense adjustments. The filing reclassified Video as held for sale and discontinued operations. By the first quarter of 2026 Harmonic had completed the French consultation, exercised the put mechanics and executed the asset purchase agreement. [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Pending sale to MediaKind](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-pending-sale-its-video-business-mediakind) [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

Seen together, the ledger Ben-Natan inherited was neither as weak nor as smooth as the draft suggested. Harmonic arrived at mid-2026 with a record 2024 still visible in the rear-view mirror, a trough year in 2025 that management tied to deployment timing, a very large single-customer concentration that remained only partly solved, a cleaned-up near-term debt profile, and a pending $145 million transaction that would leave the surviving company far more exposed to the success or failure of Broadband alone.

chapters.title: Post-Harshman quarters through Ben-Natan succession and Video announcement
chapters.body:
## Harshman's Final Reported Quarters

The draft treated Patrick Harshman's exit as if it had happened in September 2023. Harmonic's own chronology was different. Harshman was still Harmonic's chief executive when the company reported first-quarter 2024 results on 29 April 2024. On 8 April 2024 the board had announced that he would retire effective 11 June 2024, with Nimrod Ben-Natan named as successor. The transition therefore overlapped with first-quarter reporting rather than preceding it by months. [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Harmonic Q1 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2024-results/)

The operating backdrop was mixed. Full-year revenue had eased from $625.0 million in 2022 to $607.9 million in 2023, but fourth-quarter 2023 revenue of $167.1 million was a record for the company at the time and Broadband revenue in that quarter reached $115.2 million. Harshman's final earnings cadence was therefore not one of straightforward decline; it was the uneven pattern of a company whose broadband growth engine remained intact even as quarterly timing and the Video review clouded the picture. [Harmonic Q4 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2023-results)

## No Interim Bridge, Then a June 2024 Handover

Walter Jankovic did not serve as interim chief executive. He had joined Harmonic as chief financial officer in May 2023 and remained CFO through the succession process. Ben-Natan took over as president and chief executive on 11 June 2024, with Harmonic's subsequent filings disclosing his new appointment letter and Harshman's consulting agreement effective the same date. [Jankovic CFO appointment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-appoints-walter-jankovic-chief-financial-officer/) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Q2 2024 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131024000074/hlit-20240628.htm)

That distinction mattered because it made the 2024 management transition much less improvisational than the draft implied. The board signalled the move in April, kept Harshman in place through the second week of June, and handed the company to the executive already running Broadband.

## Ben-Natan's First Revenue Year

Ben-Natan's first full quarters as chief executive were materially stronger than the draft's framing suggested. Harmonic reported second-quarter 2024 revenue of $138.7 million, third-quarter revenue of $195.8 million and fourth-quarter revenue of $222.2 million, producing full-year 2024 revenue of $678.7 million, a company record. Broadband revenue was $488.2 million for the year and Video revenue was $190.5 million. [Harmonic Q2 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-second-quarter-2024-results) [Harmonic Q3 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/)

The Video narrative also changed over the year. In April 2024 Harmonic had ended the strategic review without a transaction. By December 2025 it had received MediaKind's binding offer and by March 2026 had executed the asset purchase agreement. The earnings story therefore moved from internal succession and operating execution in 2024 to portfolio simplification in 2025-2026. [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Pending sale to MediaKind](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-pending-sale-its-video-business-mediakind) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## The 2025 Trough, Then the 2026 Reset

After the record 2024, Harmonic's 2025 revenue fell to $570.8 million and continuing-operation Broadband revenue fell to $360.5 million as customers shifted deployment timing around Unified DOCSIS 4.0. Yet the end-of-year operating indicators turned sharply more constructive: fourth-quarter Broadband bookings hit $346.9 million, backlog and deferred revenue reached $573.8 million, and first-quarter 2026 Broadband revenue rose 43 per cent year on year to $121.7 million, prompting a raise in full-year Broadband guidance to $475 million-$495 million. [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

The corrected earnings story was therefore not Harshman, then a long Jankovic bridge, then Ben-Natan. It was Harshman through first-quarter 2024, a June 2024 handover directly to Ben-Natan, a record first full year under the new chief executive, then a 2025 broadband trough that management insisted was cyclical and that early-2026 orders were beginning to reverse.

chapters.title: Ben-Natan, Jankovic, segment leadership, and Gallagher-chaired board
chapters.body:
## Succession by Design, Not by Emergency

Harmonic's leadership structure at the frozen snapshot looked very different from the one described in the draft. Nimrod Ben-Natan had served as president and chief executive officer since June 2024, not since February 2024, and he had not come to Harmonic through the DiviCom transaction. The company's governance page said he joined Harmonic in 1996, became vice president of product marketing, solutions and strategy in 2007, and was appointed senior vice president and general manager of Cable Products in June 2012. Before Harmonic he had worked at Orckit Communications and earlier in the Israeli Defense Signal Corps. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

That biography mattered because it made the board's 2024 choice legible. Ben-Natan was not a turnaround outsider and not an executive imported through a legacy acquisition. He was the internal product leader most closely associated with Harmonic's broadband platform. When the board announced Harshman's retirement on 8 April 2024, it described a formal succession process supported by an external search firm but still concluded that the broadband leader was the standout candidate. [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/)

## Harshman and the Real Handover Timeline

Patrick Harshman's own chronology was also more precise than the draft allowed. Harmonic's 2006 succession release said he joined the company in 1993 and became president and chief executive in May 2006. The 2024 release said he would retire effective 11 June 2024. Harmonic's second-quarter 2024 filing then disclosed a consulting agreement with him effective the same date. That sequence meant Harshman left management in June 2024 after 18 years as CEO, but did not remain on the 2026 board roster that Harmonic published for the frozen window. [Harshman CEO appointment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-appoints-patrick-harshman-president-and-chief-executive) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Q2 2024 filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131024000074/hlit-20240628.htm) [2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000114036126016701/ny20067701x1_def14a.htm)

Walter Jankovic's role needed similar repair. Harmonic appointed him chief financial officer in May 2023. He did not serve as interim chief executive during the 2024 transition; instead he remained CFO while Harshman stayed in the top seat through June and Ben-Natan took over. [Jankovic CFO appointment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-appoints-walter-jankovic-chief-financial-officer/) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/)

## The Executive Roster as of 23 May 2026

Harmonic's governance page listed a leaner operating roster than the one in the appendix. As of the frozen snapshot, the named executive group on the site comprised Nimrod Ben-Natan as president and chief executive officer, Timothy Chu as general counsel, senior vice president of human resources and corporate secretary, Jeffrey Glahn as senior vice president of global sales, Neven Haltmayer as senior vice president and general manager, and Walter Jankovic as chief financial officer. Bart Spriester, Robert Folliard, Jay Stein and Ian Graham did not appear in the current governance roster and have therefore been removed from the appendix's dated leadership table. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

That current lineup fits the transaction stage Harmonic was in. Ben-Natan and Jankovic carried the capital-markets story; Chu sat over the legal and governance machinery needed for the pending MediaKind sale and the public-company obligations around it; Glahn represented the sales spine of a broadband business that was still trying to diversify beyond Comcast; and Haltmayer remained one of the principal named operators during the late-stage existence of the Video line. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## Gallagher's Board, Corrected

The board chapter in the draft was the most outdated part of the dossier. Harmonic's current governance materials and 2026 proxy showed a seven-member board consisting of Patrick Gallagher, Nimrod Ben-Natan, Deborah L. Clifford, Stephanie Copeland, Dana Crandall, Neel Dev and David Krall. Patrick Harshman, Mitzi Reaugh, Susan G. Swenson and E. Floyd Kvamme were not on the 2026 slate. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights) [2026 proxy](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000114036126016701/ny20067701x1_def14a.htm)

Gallagher's background also needed correction. Harmonic's governance page said he had been a director since October 2007 and was elected board chair in April 2013. It described him as a former executive vice chair and chief executive of FLAG Telecom Group and a former BT Group executive, and noted that he was lead independent director at Ciena. The draft's reference to Sprint was unsupported by Harmonic's current governance disclosure. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

The independent directors the company listed were each calibrated to a different part of the business problem. Clifford, a former Autodesk and SurveyMonkey finance executive, brought capital-markets and SaaS-transition experience. Copeland came from communications infrastructure and Zayo. Crandall brought cable and pay-television operating depth, including a prior senior role in Comcast's West division. Dev added CFO and network-infrastructure experience from Wesco, Congruex and Lumen. Krall brought technology-operating history including prior roles at Roku and Avid. [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

## What the Structure Said

The corrected leadership picture was therefore more coherent than the first draft suggested. Harmonic entered mid-2026 with a board chaired by a long-tenured telecoms operator, a chief executive who had spent nearly three decades inside the company and more than a decade running its broadband franchise, a CFO installed only since 2023 but never diverted into an interim-chief-executive detour, and a current board slate newly refreshed in 2024 around infrastructure, finance and cable operating experience. That was exactly the sort of structure one would expect for a company trying to finish a business sale while convincing investors that the remaining broadband platform deserved to be valued on its own.

chapters.title: Comcast, Charter, broader cable operators, broadcasters, and supply chain
chapters.body:
The commercial architecture around Harmonic's Broadband business was anchored by Comcast in a way the draft only partially captured. The key primary document was not a vague reference to customer concentration but the company's 2016 warrant agreement. Harmonic said on 27 September 2016 that it had entered into a warrant arrangement with Comcast under which Comcast could acquire Harmonic common stock based on specific CableOS and other product sales and deployment milestones. The associated warrant filing said Comcast could purchase up to 7,816,162 shares at an exercise price of $4.76 per share, linking Comcast's economic upside directly to CableOS adoption. [Comcast warrant agreement](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-comcast-warrant-agreement) [Warrant exhibit](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131016000104/hlit-201609268xkcomcastwar.htm)

## The Comcast Commercial Architecture

That structure mattered because later annual reports showed just how concentrated the deployment became. Harmonic's 2024 annual report said Comcast accounted for 44 per cent of 2023 net revenue, 39 per cent of 2022 net revenue and 26 per cent of 2021 net revenue. The company was not merely selling into the largest U.S. cable operator; for several years it was monetising a deployment schedule that dominated the group's income statement. [2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131025000021/hlit-20241231.htm)

The operational relationship broadened as well. In September 2025 Harmonic and Comcast said Comcast had expanded its network to more than one million new locations in 2024 and planned to exceed 1.2 million new locations by the end of 2025, using Harmonic's cOS platform together with virtual BNG, remote switches and optical-line-terminal functions to support both coax and fiber builds. By the first quarter of 2026 Harmonic said cOS had been commercially deployed with 150 customers serving 45.7 million cable modems. [Harmonic and Comcast](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-and-comcast-work-together-expand-fiber-broadband-access) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

The risk side of that same relationship was explicit in Harmonic's filings. A company whose top customer had been 44 per cent of revenue in 2023 had to live with quarterly volatility whenever deployment timing changed. The 2025 Broadband trough was the most recent example.

## Charter, Spectrum and the Broader Cable Base

The draft had been right that Charter mattered, but the more precise primary-source evidence came from Harmonic's own November 2025 release. In reporting third-quarter 2025 results, Harmonic said it had announced an expanded partnership with Spectrum on cOS, DOCSIS 4.0 Unified remote PHY devices and advanced operational tools. That was a firmer statement than the earlier draft's general reference to Charter as a major customer. [Harmonic Q3 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2025-results)

Harmonic's broader customer base also looked more diversified by 2025-2026 than the draft had specified. The company said it had won seven new broadband customers in the third quarter of 2024, six more broadband customers in the third quarter of 2025, and additional DOCSIS 4.0 and fiber wins in the first quarter of 2026. That did not erase Comcast concentration, but it did show a widening commercial funnel beyond the anchor account. [Harmonic Q3 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q3 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## International Operators

Public disclosures were also more specific on international broadband customers than the draft implied. In June 2025 Vectra, one of Poland's largest internet providers, selected Harmonic's cOS platform for multigigabit expansion, wholesale fiber and DOCSIS services, and Harmonic described the project as the world's first implementation of its PTP-less capability for distributed access architecture. In February 2026 Harmonic said izzi, Televisa's Mexican MSO, had selected cOS as part of its strategic fiber expansion. In March 2026 Harmonic said KBRO, a Taiwanese cable operator, was extending an existing cOS deployment with fiber-on-demand upgrades. [Vectra deployment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/vectra-powers-broadband-transformation-harmonic/) [izzi deployment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/izzi-accelerates-strategic-fiber-broadband-expansion-harmonic) [KBRO deployment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/kbro-leverages-harmonics-fiber-demand-solution-network-upgrades/)

Those examples mattered because they turned the international story from an abstraction into a set of named operator references spanning Europe, Latin America and Asia. They also showed Harmonic using the same control software to sell both DOCSIS evolution and fiber expansion, which helped explain management's insistence that the addressable market extended beyond a single U.S. cable cycle.

## Video Customers, More Specific Than the Draft Allowed

The draft's Video-customer section relied on broad categories where public disclosures had actually named counterparties. In February 2025 Harmonic said Akamai had selected it as the technology vendor for one of Akamai's video streaming services. In April 2026 Harmonic said DIRECTV was transforming its U.S. direct-to-home platform with Harmonic's VOS Media Software. Those did not amount to a full customer roll-call, but they were concrete named references that the earlier text had left out. [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/) [DIRECTV deployment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-enables-directv-reimagine-nationwide-dth-service/)

## Supply Chain

The supply-chain section also benefited from more specific sourcing. Harmonic's 2025 10-K said Plexus Services Corp. acted as its primary contract manufacturer and accounted for the majority of the products it purchased from contract manufacturers, with the automatically renewing agreement then running to October 2026. The same filing said many components, subassemblies and modules were sourced from sole suppliers or a limited group of suppliers and that supplier consolidation had constrained qualification of alternatives. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm)

That disclosure was more useful than speculation about merchant-silicon names because it showed the real operational dependency: Harmonic remained asset-light relative to older hardware vendors, but it still relied on a concentrated contract-manufacturing and component ecosystem. What made the model more resilient was the software layer. Because cOS ran on COTS infrastructure and increasingly supported operator-owned server footprints, Harmonic could argue that part of its commercial value lay in reducing bespoke-hardware dependency rather than deepening it. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm)

chapters.title: Where Harmonic sits against Cisco, CommScope, Vecima, Arista, and the broader cable access
chapters.body:
By the time Nimrod Ben-Natan became president and chief executive on 11 June 2024, Harmonic's competitive case rested less on analyst market-share tables than on disclosed operating scale. At fiscal 2025 year-end the company said its cOS broadband platform was commercially deployed with 146 customers serving 41 million cable modems, and in the first quarter of 2026 it raised that figure to 150 customers and 45.7 million cable modems. That did not prove the market had tipped irreversibly, but it did establish that Harmonic entered the next DOCSIS spending cycle from an installed-base position the draft dossier had understated. [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## What the primary record showed

Harmonic's 2025 10-K said the broadband market was extremely competitive but did not publish a named market-share table. CommScope's 2024 10-K was more explicit from the other side: in its Access Network Solutions segment it listed Harmonic, Cisco, Casa Systems, Technetix, Teleste, Vecima and ATX among competitors. Read together, the primary filings pointed to a narrower field than the draft suggested: a legacy Cisco installed base, a scaled CommScope access franchise trying to refresh itself, a rising Vecima software-and-node challenger, and a smaller long tail of access vendors. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm) [CommScope 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1517228/000095017025027196/comm-20241231.htm)

## CommScope: reset, then acquisition

CommScope remained the clearest scaled rival because its own filings showed both the pressure on the legacy access model and the steps it took to update it. The company's 2024 annual report said it completed the purchase of certain Casa Systems cable assets on 7 June 2024, paid $45.1 million, and integrated the acquisition into Access Network Solutions. The same filing also preserved the record of ANS write-downs already taken before that purchase: CommScope said it had recorded a $425.9 million goodwill impairment in 2023 and a $1.1196 billion impairment in 2022, citing technology shifts affecting hardware sales, bandwidth-growth trends and other operational challenges. In other words, CommScope entered the virtualised CMTS phase while still marking down assumptions from the hardware-centric era. [CommScope 2024 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1517228/000095017025043871/commscope_2024_annual_re.pdf)

The August 2025 sale announcement sharpened that reading. When CommScope agreed to sell its Connectivity and Cable Solutions segment to Amphenol for about $10.5 billion in cash, management said ANS and RUCKUS would remain focused on the next generation of network connectivity. The cable-access business was retained rather than divested. That was important: the filing showed CommScope was not abandoning the category, but concentrating its remaining case around ANS after selling a different part of the portfolio. [CommScope CCS sale filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1517228/000119312525172146/d842392dex991.htm)

## Cisco: still in the installed base, but winding down the flagship chassis

Cisco still mattered because it occupied so much of the historical CMTS footprint Harmonic had spent a decade attacking. CommScope continued to name Cisco as an ANS competitor in its 2024 10-K. But Cisco's own product bulletin showed a mature franchise moving into harvest mode rather than a fresh upgrade cycle. On 11 April 2025 Cisco announced end-of-sale and end-of-life dates for cBR-8 hardware, said the last day to order was 11 April 2026, and said there was no replacement available at that time. That did not mean every Cisco element inside cable headends vanished at once, but it did mean the signature chassis of the prior DOCSIS cycle no longer had a published hardware successor in the frozen-window record. [CommScope 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1517228/000095017025027196/comm-20241231.htm) [Cisco cBR-8 end-of-life notice](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/video/cbr-series-converged-broadband-routers/cbr-8-hardware-eol.pdf)

## Vecima: the first clearly evidenced vCMTS alternative

If CommScope represented the incumbent refreshing itself through acquisition, Vecima represented the specialist challenger moving up from distributed access. Vecima's 2024 annual information form said the company introduced Entra vCMTS on 11 March 2024 as part of its Entra Cloud platform and designed it for DOCSIS 4.0 throughput. On 15 April 2025 Vecima said Cox Communications had selected Entra vCMTS under a multi-year agreement to modernise its DOCSIS network, giving Vecima a named Tier 1 US reference inside the frozen window. [Vecima 2024 annual information form](https://vecima.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Vecima-2024-AIF-09.19.24.pdf) [Vecima Cox release](https://vecima.com/press-release/vecima-entra-vcmts-selected-by-cox-communications-to-advance-its-next-generation-docsis-network/)

The commercial ramp was still early. In its full-year fiscal 2025 results, Vecima said it had achieved first revenue from the new vCMTS product, had 136 MSO customer engagements worldwide, had 67 customers that had ordered Entra products as broader distributed-access deployment progressed, and generated $222.7 million of annual Entra DAA revenue. Gross margin for the year fell to 38.3 per cent from 48.7 per cent, a reminder that the transition remained operationally messy even as the product set broadened. The same release described Vecima as one of three vendors worldwide offering a vCMTS solution. Primary disclosures therefore showed Vecima as the first clearly evidenced alternative platform vendor in the virtualised field, but also as one still at the beginning of commercial scale relative to Harmonic's disclosed footprint. [Vecima FY2025 results](https://vecima.com/press-release/vecima-reports-q4-and-full-year-fiscal-2025-results/)

## Arista: adjacency rather than direct competition

Arista belonged in the dossier only as infrastructure adjacency. Primary filings reviewed before 23 May 2026 did not name Arista as a direct CMTS, vCMTS or distributed-access competitor to Harmonic. The frozen-window record contained no Harmonic-Arista bidding contest, named customer replacement, or product-roadmap link that justified treating Arista as a first-order competitor in cable access. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm) [CommScope 2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1517228/000095017025027196/comm-20241231.htm) [Vecima 2024 annual information form](https://vecima.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Vecima-2024-AIF-09.19.24.pdf)

## The regulatory wall around Huawei and ZTE

Chinese vendors were more a regulatory constraint than an active US contract threat inside the window. The Federal Communications Commission's 2022 order implementing the Secure Equipment Act said equipment produced by Huawei and ZTE was on the Covered List and prohibited future equipment authorisations for such covered gear. Later FCC notices continued to list both vendors. That did not erase Huawei or ZTE from overseas broadband markets, but it materially narrowed the realistic vendor shortlist for US cable operators during the DOCSIS 4.0 and fibre-upgrade cycle. [FCC Secure Equipment Act order](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/FCC-22-84A1_Rcd.pdf) [FCC Covered List notice](https://docs.fcc.gov/public/attachments/DA-24-886A1.pdf)

| Vendor | What the primary record showed by 23 May 2026 | Competitive read-through |
|---|---|---|
| Harmonic | 150 cOS customers and 45.7 million cable modems in Q1 2026; 146 customers and 41 million modems at 2025 year-end [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) | Only vendor in the dossier's primary-source set disclosing commercial scale in the tens of millions of managed modems |
| CommScope | Casa cable assets acquired for $45.1 million on 7 June 2024; ANS retained when CCS sale was announced in August 2025 [CommScope 2024 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1517228/000095017025043871/commscope_2024_annual_re.pdf) [CommScope CCS sale filing](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1517228/000119312525172146/d842392dex991.htm) | Still a real incumbent, but one that bought part of its virtualised response and kept access as a remaining core business |
| Vecima | Entra vCMTS launched in March 2024; Cox win announced in April 2025; first vCMTS revenue reported in fiscal 2025 [Vecima 2024 annual information form](https://vecima.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/09/Vecima-2024-AIF-09.19.24.pdf) [Vecima Cox release](https://vecima.com/press-release/vecima-entra-vcmts-selected-by-cox-communications-to-advance-its-next-generation-docsis-network/) [Vecima FY2025 results](https://vecima.com/press-release/vecima-reports-q4-and-full-year-fiscal-2025-results/) | Most clearly evidenced alternative entrant, but still early in revenue and deployment scale |
| Cisco | cBR-8 hardware end-of-sale announced 11 April 2025; last order date 11 April 2026; no replacement available at that time [Cisco cBR-8 end-of-life notice](https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/products/collateral/video/cbr-series-converged-broadband-routers/cbr-8-hardware-eol.pdf) | Legacy installed base remained relevant, but the flagship hardware platform was being wound down |

Set against that record, Harmonic's lead was better described as a disclosed scale advantage than as a permanently settled market-share verdict. CommScope still had the customer relationships and balance-sheet motivation to stay in the fight, and Vecima had finally produced a named Tier 1 US vCMTS award. But within the frozen window, only Harmonic disclosed a platform already serving tens of millions of cable modems at commercial scale. That was the structural gap the market was actually underwriting. [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/) [CommScope 2024 annual report](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1517228/000095017025043871/commscope_2024_annual_re.pdf) [Vecima FY2025 results](https://vecima.com/press-release/vecima-reports-q4-and-full-year-fiscal-2025-results/)

chapters.title: From 1995 IPO through CableOS, Harshman retirement, Ben-Natan succession, Video separation
chapters.body:
## Founding and Listing

Harmonic said in its 2025 annual report that it was initially incorporated in California in June 1988, reincorporated in Delaware in May 1995 and had been listed on Nasdaq since its initial public offering in 1995. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm)

## Harshman Era: 2006-2024

Patrick Harshman joined Harmonic in 1993 and became president and chief executive officer in May 2006. His tenure covered the later video-infrastructure years, the CableOS build-out and the first large-scale Comcast monetisation phase. The board announced on 8 April 2024 that he would retire effective 11 June 2024. [Harshman CEO appointment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-appoints-patrick-harshman-president-and-chief-executive) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/)

## CableOS, Comcast and the Broadband Pivot

A pivotal milestone came with the September 2016 Comcast warrant agreement tied to CableOS deployment milestones. Commercial scale followed over the next several years, with Harmonic's revenue rising from $378.8 million in 2020 to $625.0 million in 2022 and then to a record $678.7 million in 2024 as Broadband became the dominant growth segment. [Comcast warrant agreement](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-comcast-warrant-agreement) [2021 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131022000012/hlit-20211231.htm) [Harmonic Q4 2022 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2022-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/)

## Leadership Transition

The succession occurred in two steps: announcement on 8 April 2024, effective handover on 11 June 2024. Nimrod Ben-Natan, who had joined Harmonic in 1996 and led Broadband since 2012, became chief executive directly; Walter Jankovic remained chief financial officer rather than serving as an interim CEO. [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Harmonic governance](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/corporate-governance/highlights)

## Video Review, Then MediaKind

The board initiated a formal strategic review of the Video business in October 2023 and concluded it in April 2024 without a transaction. Only on 8 December 2025 did Harmonic disclose MediaKind's binding offer and the related put-option structure for a sale at roughly $145 million in cash. By March 2026 the asset purchase agreement had been executed, and by May 2026 Harmonic still expected a second-quarter close. [Harmonic Q3 2023 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-third-quarter-2023-results) [Harmonic CEO succession](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-ceo-succession/) [Pending sale to MediaKind](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-pending-sale-its-video-business-mediakind) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

chapters.title: CableOS virtualisation, DOCSIS 4.0 support, broader patents
chapters.body:
## The Virtual Stack

Harmonic's broadband technology disclosures during the frozen window described cOS as a software-based virtualized broadband platform running on commercial off-the-shelf servers and connected to distributed access nodes. That was the core architectural claim behind the company's investment case: broadband-access intelligence could be moved into software and then evolved across DOCSIS and fiber without relying on proprietary CMTS chassis refreshes. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm) [Harmonic Extends Lead in Virtualized Broadband](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-extends-lead-virtualized-broadband/)

Harmonic's own 2023 broadband release supplied the cleanest sourced efficiency metric. It said that density and performance improvements across seven generations of commercial servers had produced a 75 per cent reduction in power consumption since 2016. The draft's 20-to-1 rack-footprint claim was not supported by the primary materials reviewed and has been removed. [Harmonic Extends Lead in Virtualized Broadband](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-extends-lead-virtualized-broadband/)

## Patent Base

The foundational patent claim was supported. On 26 July 2018 Harmonic announced that the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office had granted Patent No. 10,020,962, covering the "Virtual Converged Cable Access Platform (CCAP) Core". Harmonic presented that grant as recognition of the virtualization architecture behind CableOS. [CableOS patent grant](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-awarded-key-patent-cableostm-virtualized-cable-access)

By the 2025 annual report, Harmonic said it held 65 issued U.S. patents, seven issued foreign patents and 39 patent applications pending as of 31 December 2025. The draft's count was correct, but it needed a proper primary citation. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm)

## Unified DOCSIS 4.0 and Fiber Convergence

The most important product milestone in the recent record was Harmonic's move to unified DOCSIS 4.0. On 17 October 2023 the company said cOS, the successor brand to CableOS, supported both full-duplex and extended-spectrum DOCSIS 4.0, as well as 10G fiber, inside a single platform. A year later Harmonic and Comcast said they would demonstrate the industry's first unified DOCSIS 4.0 and fiber solution at SCTE TechExpo24. In July 2025 Harmonic said its cOS platform and Pebble-2 device had achieved 14 Gbps downstream throughput at a CableLabs interoperability event. [Harmonic Extends Lead in Virtualized Broadband](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-extends-lead-virtualized-broadband/) [Comcast and Harmonic at SCTE TechExpo24](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/comcast-and-harmonic-demonstrate-industrys-first-unified-docsis/) [14 Gbps DOCSIS 4.0 record](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-sets-docsis-40-record-14-gbps-downstream-speed)

Field references followed. In August 2024 Harmonic said Mediacom had adopted its Unified DOCSIS 4.0 platform. In September 2025 Harmonic and Mediacom said they would show a production deployment on a live network at SCTE TechExpo25. [Mediacom deployment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/mediacom-communications-leads-broadband-innovation-unified/) [Harmonic and Mediacom milestone](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-and-mediacom-mark-industry-milestone-unified-docsis-40/)

## Timing, PTP-less Operation and Newer Intelligence Layers

The PTP-less timing claims were also better documented than the draft implied. Harmonic's first-quarter 2025 results said major broadband innovations in production included its PTP-less timing solution, which management said enabled higher reliability and lower operating costs. In June 2025 Harmonic said Poland's Vectra had selected the company for what it described as the world's first implementation of Harmonic's PTP-less capability in a live distributed-access deployment. [Harmonic Q1 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2025-results/) [Vectra deployment](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/vectra-powers-broadband-transformation-harmonic/)

By the frozen window Harmonic had also started using more explicit language around intelligent network operations. Its April and May 2026 broadband announcements for the FTTH Conference and ANGA COM described AI-powered network-operations intelligence as part of the next cOS-era toolkit. Those releases did not amount to a mature revenue line, but they did show that the company had begun commercial messaging around automation and network intelligence rather than leaving the theme as outside speculation. [FTTH Conference 2026 preview](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-unveil-breakthrough-fiber-innovations-ftth-conference/) [ANGA COM 2026](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-defines-new-era-broadband-connectivity-anga-com-2026)

## Litigation and R&D

The draft's Avid paragraph was broadly right and could be sourced more tightly. Harmonic's first-quarter 2018 10-Q said that Avid had first sued in October 2011, that the parties settled on 19 October 2017 by entering into a settlement and patent-portfolio cross-license agreement, and that the consolidated cases were dismissed with prejudice. Harmonic's fiscal-2018 earnings materials separately said the company agreed to pay Avid a one-time $6 million amount in installments, with $2.5 million paid upfront in October 2017 and the balance due in 2019 and 2020. [Q1 2018 10-Q](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000851310/000085131018000033/hlit-20180330x10q.htm) [Harmonic Q4 2018 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2018-results)

R&D spending also remained substantial. Harmonic's 2023 annual report said research-and-development expense was about $126.3 million in 2023; the 2024 annual report put 2024 R&D at $121.0 million. Those figures helped explain why the board's eventual decision was to sell Video only after Broadband had amassed enough scale and technical differentiation to stand on its own. [2023 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131024000024/hlit-20231231.htm) [2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131025000021/hlit-20241231.htm)

chapters.title: Comcast concentration, DOCSIS 4.0 cycle, competitive intensity, Video separation execution
chapters.body:
## A Narrowing Base, an Unsettled Industry

The post-sale Harmonic that management was describing by May 2026 would be simpler than the historic company, but it would also be less diversified. The principal risk vectors were clearer once the chronology and revenue figures were corrected.

## The Comcast Dependency

The single largest risk remained customer concentration. Harmonic's 2024 annual report said Comcast represented 44 per cent of 2023 net revenue, 39 per cent of 2022 net revenue and 26 per cent of 2021 net revenue. That scale explained why the Broadband step-up was so powerful and why 2025 timing changes were so painful. If Comcast slowed deployment or changed vendor strategy, Harmonic would feel it quickly. [2024 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000085131025000021/hlit-20241231.htm)

## DOCSIS 4.0 Cycle Timing

The second risk was not whether DOCSIS 4.0 existed but whether the spend arrived on Harmonic's timetable. Harmonic's own disclosures showed Broadband revenue rising to $488.2 million in 2024, falling to $360.5 million in 2025 continuing operations, then being guided back up to $475 million-$495 million for 2026 as backlog rebuilt. That was the signature of a capital cycle whose timing was still customer-controlled. [Harmonic Q4 2024 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2024-results/) [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## Competitive Intensity

The third risk was that Harmonic was no longer alone in virtualized cable access. Harmonic's own materials highlighted growth in deployments and customer counts, but operators were also expanding qualification work across multiple vendors and technologies. The practical consequence was not necessarily sudden share loss; it was more often pricing pressure, slower rollout pacing and the need to keep spending heavily on interoperability, timing simplification and DOCSIS-and-fiber convergence.

## Video Sale Execution

The fourth risk sat inside the transaction itself. Harmonic's first-quarter 2026 results said the French works-council process had been completed, the asset purchase agreement had been signed on 20 March 2026, and either party could terminate if conditions were not met by 8 June 2026, subject to extension to 8 September 2026 under certain circumstances. That meant the sale was advanced, but not done, by the frozen date. [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## Supply Chain and Execution

The fifth risk was operational. Harmonic's 2025 annual report said Plexus was its primary contract manufacturer and that many components and subassemblies came from sole or limited suppliers. A software-led model reduced some hardware burden, but it did not eliminate execution risk if component or contract-manufacturing bottlenecks re-emerged. [2025 10-K](https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/851310/000119312526067506/hlit-20251231.htm)

## Optionality That Was Still Only Optionality

The sixth risk was narrative inflation. Harmonic's spring-2026 product releases had begun talking about AI-powered network-operations intelligence, but those releases did not yet show a separately disclosed revenue stream or a proven margin contribution from that layer. Investors could legitimately assign option value to the software stack; they could not yet treat that option as booked business. [FTTH Conference 2026 preview](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-unveil-breakthrough-fiber-innovations-ftth-conference/) [ANGA COM 2026](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-defines-new-era-broadband-connectivity-anga-com-2026)

chapters.title: DOCSIS 4.0 transition, Video separation completion, AI routing optionality
chapters.body:
## The Pure-Play Pivot

By the frozen snapshot date, Harmonic was close to becoming the company management had only hinted at in 2024: a broadband-only platform vendor with Video held for sale. The transaction was not yet closed, but the works-council process had been completed, the asset purchase agreement had been signed on 20 March 2026, and Harmonic still expected the sale to MediaKind for about $145 million in cash to close in the second quarter. [Pending sale to MediaKind](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-pending-sale-its-video-business-mediakind) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/)

## DOCSIS 4.0 and Fiber: The Demand Thesis

The operating case rested on a backlog-supported rebound in Broadband. Harmonic ended 2025 with $573.8 million of backlog and deferred revenue, lifted that to $582.1 million in the first quarter of 2026, and raised full-year Broadband guidance to $475 million-$495 million after reporting 43 per cent year-on-year Broadband growth in the quarter. cOS had reached 150 commercial customers and 45.7 million cable modems by then, while the company's spring-2026 releases also leaned harder into fiber convergence. [Harmonic Q4 2025 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-fourth-quarter-and-fiscal-2025-results) [Harmonic Q1 2026 results](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-announces-first-quarter-2026-results/) [ANGA COM 2026](https://investor.harmonicinc.com/news-releases/news-release-details/harmonic-defines-new-era-broadband-connectivity-anga-com-2026)

## What Remained Unproven

What remained unresolved was diversification. Comcast still dominated the installed base and the historical revenue mix, and the 2025 trough showed how exposed Harmonic remained to a handful of operator calendars. The newer international wins, the Spectrum expansion, and the AI-powered operations narrative all pointed in the right direction, but the central proof still had to come from a broader set of paying broadband deployments after the Video business left the perimeter.

leadership.key_finding: Harmonic's executive structure reflects the strategic transformation through 2023-2024 from Patrick Harshman's long-tenured CEO leadership (1997-2023) through the interim Jankovic CEO bridge into Nimrod Ben-Natan's February 2024 succession. Ben-Natan, who joined Harmonic through the 1999 acquisition of his company DiviCom and subsequently held multiple senior roles including President of the Cable Edge business, brings deep CableOS-product-line continuity to the CEO role at the moment when the Broadband segment is scaling through the multi-year DOCSIS 4.0 cycle and the Video segment is being prepared for separation. The CFO function under Walter Jankovic (returned to CFO role following Ben-Natan's CEO succession, having previously held interim CEO during the post-Harshman transition) provides operational continuity. The board is chaired by Patrick Gallagher (since 2022) and includes long-tenured directors plus the additions calibrated to the evolving business profile.
